grammar.title: 1B: Future forms - present continuous, be going to, will / won't
grammar.explanation:
Use **be going to** + verb for a plan you already decided. I am going to bake the cake from my new recipe.

Use **be going to** + verb for a prediction with evidence. The water is hot, so it is going to boil soon.

Use **am / is / are** + verb-**ing** for a future arrangement. I am meeting Sara on Friday to buy ingredients.

Use **will** + verb for a decision you make right now. The soup is too salty, so I will add water and stir it.

Use **will** + verb for a promise or an offer. I will help you chop the onions, and I will peel the potatoes.

**Won't** means will not. I won't fry the eggs, but I will taste the vegetables.
examples: I *am going to bake* a cake tomorrow. (a plan - already decided)
Look! The water *is going to boil* soon. (a prediction with evidence)
She *is going to fry* the eggs for breakfast. (a plan - already decided)
We *are meeting* Sara on Friday to buy ingredients. (a future arrangement)
I *am peeling* potatoes with my mother tonight. (a future arrangement)
I *am chopping* onions with Ali tomorrow morning. (a future arrangement)
The soup is too salty. I *will add* some water. (an instant decision)
I *will help* you stir the soup. (an offer)
I *will taste* the cake from this recipe and tell you my opinion. (a promise)
I *won't fry* the fish; I *will boil* the vegetables. (negative + instant decision)

practice.q: You decided yesterday to bake a cake on Saturday. Which is correct: 'I bake a cake' or 'I am going to bake a cake'?
practice.a: 'I am going to bake a cake on Saturday.' - a plan you already decided.

practice.q: The phone rings and you decide NOW to answer it. Which is correct: 'I answer it' or 'I will answer it'?
practice.a: 'I will answer it.' - an instant decision.

practice.q: You fixed a time with your friend to cook together on Sunday. Which is correct: 'We cook together' or 'We are cooking together'?
practice.a: 'We are cooking together on Sunday.' - a future arrangement.
